title: Data Engineer
tagline: Build the pipelines and warehouses that every data and AI team depends on.
about: Data engineers move, clean, model and serve data at scale. Without reliable pipelines there's no analytics, no machine learning and no AI. You'll design warehouses, write transformations, orchestrate jobs and make sure data is correct, fresh and cheap to query.
It's backend engineering with a data focus, and demand has grown steadily with AI.

phases.title: Programming foundations
phases.goal: Write small programs confidently and use the tools every developer uses daily.

nodes.d: Pick Python and get fluent with the basics before anything else. Fluency in one language transfers to every other.
links: CS50x: Harvard's intro to computer science

nodes.d: Developers live in the command line: navigating files, running programs and chaining tools together.
links: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (MIT)
OverTheWire: Bandit (learn the shell by playing)

nodes.d: Version control is non-negotiable: every job uses it. Commit early, branch for experiments, open pull requests.
Break problems down, read errors calmly, use a debugger and print statements deliberately.
links: Exercism: practice in 70+ languages with mentoring

phases.title: SQL & data modelling
phases.goal: Become excellent at SQL and at designing tables.

nodes.d: Window functions, CTEs, and set-based thinking.
links: Use The Index, Luke: SQL indexing

nodes.d: Normalised models for apps, dimensional models for analytics.
Columnar storage, lakehouses and file formats.
A fast analytical database you can run on a laptop.

phases.title: Pipelines
phases.goal: Move data reliably from sources to consumers.

nodes.d: Extract, load, transform: where the transformation happens and why it moved into the warehouse.
Catch bad data before it reaches dashboards.
Snowflake, BigQuery or Redshift, and their cost models.

project.d: Ingest a public API daily, load to a warehouse (or DuckDB), model it with dbt (staging → marts), add tests and docs, orchestrate with Airflow, and build a dashboard on top.

phases.title: Big data & streaming
phases.goal: When data doesn't fit on one machine or can't wait for tomorrow.

nodes.d: Process terabytes with DataFrames across a cluster.
Event logs, consumers and stream processing.
Access control, lineage, PII and compliance.
Feature stores, embeddings pipelines and vector stores.

project.d: Stream events through Kafka into a warehouse with a Spark or Flink job, exactly-once semantics where possible, and a live dashboard with freshness alerts.

interview: Design a pipeline: sources, modelling, orchestration, quality, failure handling.
Explain partitioning, file formats and when to use streaming.
